Text:
PETALING JAYA: PAS is expected to let Perikatan Nasional (PN) go dormant without formally dissolving it as cooperation with Umno and Bersatu is no longer viewed as a viable option, according to a political scientist.

Wong Chin Huat of Sunway University said PAS now appears ready to shift course and build a new coalition with the Reset movement led by Hamzah Zainudin, as well as Pejuang and Berjasa.

He said cooperation with Umno and Bersatu was impossible as the two parties were large enough to become significant rivals, likening the three-way dynamic to rival suitors.

“The advantage of Pejuang and Berjasa is that they are small and insignificant. As such, they are likely to accept whatever PAS offers in exchange for projecting an image of Malay-Muslim unity,” he told FMT.

Wong added that such a coalition would also free PAS from negotiating seat allocations with Bersatu, while allowing its new allies to contest against Bersatu on their own terms.

He was commenting on remarks by PAS treasurer Iskandar Abdul Samad, who suggested that a coalition comprising PAS, Pejuang, Berjasa and Reset could provide the most stable platform to advance the Malay-Muslim agenda.

However, Iskandar said such cooperation would likely face attempts to undermine it, without elaborating further.

Azmil Tayeb of Universiti Sains Malaysia said that PAS sees itself as capable of operating independently, or alongside other parties or movements, having realised that losing Bersatu would not significantly affect it.

He said this was evident during the last general election (GE15), when Bersatu was shown to be heavily dependent on PAS’s grassroots machinery to remain electorally competitive.

“It would resemble the GE14 model, where PAS worked with smaller parties like Berjasa to form the Gagasan Sejahtera coalition, yet still managed to win 18 parliamentary seats at the time,” he said.

Azmil also said Umno’s preference for contesting solo, overlapping traditional seats, and a complex political history between the parties would make any post-PN cooperation difficult.

“Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama), meanwhile, has a different ideology because its struggle is not rooted in Malay-Islam supremacy,” he said.

Rafizi Ramli and Nik Nazmi have officially resigned from PKR, vacated their seats in Pandan and Setiawangsa, and taken leadership of Party Bersama Malaysia. 

This marks a bold and necessary break from the endless cycle of Malaysian politics.

Enough is enough.

For far too long, Malaysian politics has been trapped in a tired rotation between PH (DAP, PKR, AMANAH), BN (UMNO, MCA, MIC), and PN (PAS, BERSATU). 

Every election feels like a repeat: the same faces, the same coalitions, the same disappointments. 

Are you not bored? 
Are you not tired? 
Are you not disappointed?

Old politics. Old mindset.

Today, we say NO.

The Racial Arithmetic is Brutal but Real 
Betty Teh | Malaysian Politics 

Malaysian elections are still heavily ethnicised. 

The Malay vote fractures between UMNO, Bersatu, PAS, and now potentially PKR and Bersama. The Chinese and Indian votes function largely as a defensive bloc gravitating toward whichever side appears most viable against conservative dominance. 

In this landscape, any new entrant risks being labelled a spoiler before it fields a single candidate. The cynics are already sharpening their pens. Another party, they say. Another split. Another gift to Perikatan Nasional wrapped in idealism and delivered to PAS on a silver platter. 

This fear is not irrational. 

In a First-Past-The-Post system, a 10% swing in a marginal seat is not a footnote, it is a verdict. 

Critics paint the scenario with uncomfortable precision: Bersama draws educated moderate voters from both communities who previously backed PH, the consolidated Malay Muslim right sails through the middle, and the progressive camp loses seats it could have held by simply staying together. 

The Sheraton Move trauma runs deep. Non Malay voters in particular remember watching coalitions fracture and reform with alarming frequency, each time extracting a democratic price paid by ordinary people while politicians renegotiated their positions behind closed doors. 

The instinct to consolidate to hold your nose and vote for the least bad option is not cowardice. It is hard won wisdom from a decade of watching fragmentation serve the wrong side. 

But here is what the cynics’ argument quietly assumes — that PH, left undisturbed, would have held those seats anyway. That the disillusionment driving voters toward Parti Bersama is Bersama’s creation rather than PH’s inheritance. 

That a party which failed to repeal the Sedition Act, renewed Azam Baki’s contract three times, opened criminal investigations against Bloomberg for reporting what was already in the public domain, and watched its own Youth chief call for investigations into civil society using the language of national security threats — would somehow have retained the progressive vote through sheer incumbency. 

Bersama did not create the fracture. It emerged from it. 

The split happened the moment PH chose accommodation over accountability. 

Rafizi and Nik Nazmi are not the cause of progressive exhaustion. They are its most visible symptom. 

The deeper question is whether Malaysian democracy can afford to remain hostage to racial arithmetic indefinitely. 

Every election cycle the argument is the same — not now, not this time, the stakes are too high, hold the line, we cannot risk it. 

And every cycle the parties that benefit from this logic grow more comfortable taking their voters for granted precisely because those voters have nowhere else to go. 

A captive vote is a devalued vote. The moment you guarantee your support regardless of performance, you have surrendered your leverage entirely. 

What Bersama offers whatever its electoral prospects is the restoration of that leverage. 

It tells PH that progressive voters have a choice. And parties that face genuine competition tend, over time, to govern better than those that do not. 

I joined Parti Bersama Malaysia as an ordinary member. Not because I believe it will win GE16 decisively, nobody credible is claiming that. But because I believe Malaysia needs a politics where ideas compete, where voters are not guilt tripped into perpetual loyalty to imperfect coalitions, and where the argument for change does not always have to wait for a safer moment that never comes. 

The racial arithmetic is brutal but real — and the only way to change it is to stop organising exclusively around it. 

That is what Bersama is attempting. 

Messily, imperfectly, with limited machinery and considerable courage. 

Whether it succeeds or fails, the attempt itself is necessary. A democracy that punishes people for trying to build something new is not protecting reform. It is rationing it.

Two New Parties, Two Different Worlds — Malaysia's Political Landscape Cracks Open
Betty Teh | Malaysian Politics 
18 May 2026

On the same Sunday that Pakatan Harapan held its first convention in four years in Johor Bahru, gathering under the theme "Tekad Madani, Harapan Rakyat" to project unity ahead of GE16; two of its most prominent former ministers were in Petaling Jaya doing something the convention was specifically designed to prevent.

History, as it turns out, did not check the convention schedule.

The Method: How You Build a Party Without Building a Party

At the PJ Performing Arts Centre on Sunday 17 May 2026, Parti Bersama Malaysia founder and president Tan Gin Theam handed the party's registration certificate to Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli and Nik Nazmi in front of more than 3,000 supporters. No new party was formed. No ROS application was filed. No years of bureaucratic purgatory endured. 

They simply took over what already existed.

Parti Bersama Malaysia also known as the Malaysian United Party, or Parti MU was registered in Penang on 2 December 2016. It was established as a third force intended to serve as a check and balance on both government and opposition. In its entire existence before Sunday, it had contested seats and lost its deposits. It was, in the most technical sense, a registered political party. And in Malaysian politics, that registration is worth more than any election result. 

This is not a new playbook. PKR itself was born from the shell of Parti Rakyat Malaysia in 1999, when Anwar Ibrahim's Reformasi movement needed a registered vehicle fast. PSM fought for ten years to get its own registration. The lesson every serious Malaysian political operator has learned is the same: do not fight the Registrar of Societies. Find someone who already won that fight and buy their house.

Rafizi and Nik Nazmi found a ten year old house in Penang for the price of a handshake and a ceremony.

Why They Did It — The Kamikaze Calculation

Rafizi called the takeover their "second kamikaze mission." "We know there is no guarantee we will succeed. We might lose our deposits in every seat and be laughed at," he said to 2,000 supporters who responded with the kind of noise that suggests they did not find it funny at all. 

"Every day people ask, what has happened? Why are Pakatan and PKR like this? Why are Pakatan betraying their core principles and repeating the same mistakes we elected them to fix? It is hard to answer," said Nik Nazmi. 

The answer they have chosen is not to answer but to leave. 

They vacate their seats. They return their mandates. They ask the rakyat to choose again under a new banner. Whatever one thinks of the politics, the gesture is unambiguous. These are not men hopping toward safety. These are men jumping off a cliff and hoping the parachute opens on the way down.

The five PKR MPs who attended the event: Wong Chen, Bakhtiar Wan Chik, Rodziah Ismail, Zahir Hassan, and Lee Chean Chung are now under PKR membership review. Their silence since Sunday is the loudest sound in Malaysian politics right now. 

The next 72 hours will tell us whether Bersama is a movement or a moment. 

Now Enter the Other Man

While Rafizi builds his new platform on reform and democratic principle, a very different kind of political reconstruction is happening on the other side of the aisle. And the architect is a man who is less nyet nyet nyet compared ti Rafizi.

Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainuddin. MP for Larut since 2008. Former Home Minister. Former BERSATU deputy president. Former Leader of the Opposition. Widely described in political circles as "the Lord of Darkness", an operator who works entirely in the shadows, building networks and pulling levers that others only discover after the fact. 

If Rafizi is a man who announces his moves on a stage to 3,000 people, Hamzah is a man whose next move remains deliberately undefined yet the vehicle he is moving toward may turn out to be more structurally solid than anything Rafizi has just acquired.

The Sacking — And the War Inside BERSATU 

On 13 February 2026, Hamzah was expelled from BERSATU by its disciplinary board alongside 16 other members, all aligned with Hamzah in what had been a bitter internal power struggle against party president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin.

The accusation was straightforward; Hamzah had plotted to challenge Muhyiddin's leadership. The counter accusation, from Hamzah's camp, was that Muhyiddin's allies including BERSATU secretary general Mohamed Azmin Ali had orchestrated the purge to eliminate a rival power bloc that had grown too large to ignore.

What is not disputed is the arithmetic. BERSATU began with 31 MPs. Six left to become pro government independents. 

Eighteen chose to stand with Hamzah. Only six remained with Muhyiddin. The man expelled from the party had more of its parliamentary members behind him than the man who did the expelling. 

Despite being sacked from BERSATU, Hamzah retained his Leader of the Opposition position, the role is determined by parliamentary arithmetic, not party membership. He resigned in April 2026 and was replaced by Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar of PAS. 

Three False Starts and One Reverse Trojan Horse

Finding a political home was not straightforward. Hamzah outlined three options at a briefing on 14 February 2026: take over Parti Berjasa Malaysia, return to UMNO, or join PAS. 

Parti Keluarga Malaysia, a 90% confirmed deal collapsed when it emerged the party's ROS registration had been rejected in 2022 and remained legally unregistered. UMNO was complicated by its unity government association with DAP, which Hamzah's Malay nationalist base finds politically toxic.

Which brings us to the Reverse Trojan Horse.

Berjasa, formerly known as Barisan Jemaah Islamiah Se-Malaysia, was founded in 1977 as a PAS splinter party. It won 11 seats in the 1978 Kelantan state elections and has been largely dormant since. But it has a national division structure going back nearly 50 years, has already been accepted into Perikatan Nasional as an affiliate member alongside Pejuang, and has strategically rebranded as Parti Berjasa Malaysia, opening its membership to non Muslims. 

The genius of the Berjasa move is its impact on BERSATU. With 19 MPs behind him, a Hamzah led Berjasa instantly becomes the second largest party in PN, dwarfing BERSATU's remaining six. Muhyiddin faces an impossible choice: remain in PN and watch his archrival displace him as the coalition's second force, or leave PN and destroy his own political relevance. 

The announcement is expected before end of May.

The Surprising Openness to Non Malays

Perhaps the most counterintuitive element of Hamzah's repositioning is his apparent willingness to build a multiracial vehicle. For a man whose entire career has been rooted in Malay nationalist politics; UMNO, then BERSATU, then PN — the opening of Berjasa to non Muslim membership is a significant departure from type.

The rationale is partly practical, his expelled allies from Sabah and Sarawak, Ronald Kiandee and Ali Biju, are non Muslim Bumiputera who need a legal home. A Malay only party cannot accommodate them. 

But there is a deeper strategic calculation. A Berjasa that is technically open to all races while remaining culturally and organisationally Malay in its leadership and base gives Hamzah the ability to contest seats across a broader demographic spectrum without triggering the racial branding that limits seat allocation negotiations within PN. It is the same logic Gerakan used for five decades; nominally multiracial, practically ethnically defined. The label serves electoral arithmetic even when the reality tells a different story.

Two Parties, Two Directions, One Fracturing Landscape

Sunday 17 May 2026 will be remembered as the day Malaysian politics cracked visibly along two fault lines simultaneously.

On one side, Rafizi and Nik Nazmi men of the reformist left, building on transparency, democratic sacrifice, and a Penang Chinese party shell heading toward a hung parliament scenario where a clean reform bloc could serve as kingmaker.

On the other, Hamzah the operator of the shadows, a man with 19 MPs, a hundred division chiefs, and PAS's quiet blessing reaching for a 1977 Islamic splinter party and rebranding it as something new enough to contest GE16 but old enough to walk straight into PN without knocking.

Both men are doing the same thing. Recycling the past into the future because Malaysia's political architecture gives them no other choice.

The difference is the direction they are facing.

Rafizi faces the voters. Hamzah faces the coalition.

In 72 hours we will know which strategy the Speaker validates. In GE16 we will know which one Malaysia chooses.

OPINION | Perikatan Does Not Need Another Caretaker — It Needs a Founder

What exactly is PAS’s problem with Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin?

Is it the issue involving his son-in-law?

Is it the numerous court cases hanging over his head?

Is it Tun Dr Mahathir’s allegation that Muhyiddin siphoned money from Bersatu?

No.

PAS’s chief problem with Muhyiddin is far simpler, and far more fundamental: under his leadership, Perikatan Nasional is losing.

Not only is Perikatan failing to win new ground, it cannot even hold on to what it already has. Election after election, by-election after by-election, the trend has been unmistakable — Perikatan is bleeding support, slowly but steadily, and the passage of time has only worsened its condition.

What alarms PAS even more is not merely the losing, but Muhyiddin’s response to the losing — or rather, the lack of it.

1) A Leader Without Urgency

Why do I say Muhyiddin does not seem concerned?

Because there is no sense of urgency about him at all.

When an organisation has been on a downward trajectory for nearly three years, one would expect its leader to be visibly agitated — pushing reforms, making drastic changes, reshuffling leadership, rethinking strategy. One would expect frustration, anger, or at the very least, urgency.

Instead, Muhyiddin remains calm. Almost serenely so.

Perikatan has gone from good to bad, and from bad to worse, yet its chairman appears entirely unperturbed. Having Muhyiddin as PN’s leader is like having the captain of a ship who remains composed and dignified even when it is obvious that the vessel is taking on water and sinking.

2) A Temperament Mismatched to the Moment

Why does Muhyiddin project this undisturbed calm?

The charitable explanation is that this is simply his nature. He may have been born with such a temperament, or cultivated it over decades in politics because he believes it projects dignity and statesmanship.

And under different circumstances, that disposition might indeed be admirable.

If Perikatan had already governed for a decade or two, delivered prosperity, stability, and public satisfaction — and Muhyiddin was merely the next custodian of an established legacy — his calm, gentlemanly demeanour might have been ideal.

In such a scenario, Muhyiddin could have played the Lee Hsien Loong role.

Lee Kuan Yew had already built Singapore. The foundations were firm, the structure complete. Lee Hsien Loong was not expected to reinvent the nation, only to preserve and manage what already existed. His calm competence was sufficient because the heavy lifting had already been done.

Similarly, had Muhyiddin succeeded Mahathir in the early 2000s, when UMNO’s legacy was still intact and governance was relatively stable, he might have performed adequately as a legacy carrier.

But that is not today’s reality.

3) Perikatan Does Not Need a Caretaker — It Needs a Founder

Perikatan Nasional does not need a legacy carrier.

It needs a legacy creator.

It needs a leader who can fight from a position of disadvantage, withstand pressure, outmanoeuvre Pakatan Harapan, and claw its way back to Putrajaya. Only after winning can Perikatan begin to think about continuity and refinement.

In short, Perikatan needs a Lee Kuan Yew, not a Lee Hsien Loong.

Just as Singapore would likely have been swallowed by Malaysia or Indonesia had it been led by Lee Hsien Loong at its most vulnerable moment, Perikatan too risks collapse if it continues to face Anwar Ibrahim and PH with a leader whose greatest strength is calm resignation.

4) The Dr Samsuri Speculation — And Why It Misses the Point

This brings us to the recent photograph that has reignited speculation over Perikatan’s future leadership.

Earlier this week, a photo surfaced showing former PN chairman Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin meeting Terengganu Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar. The image, shared on Facebook by Bachok MP Mohd Syahir Che Sulaiman — political secretary to PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang — was accompanied by the caption: “Alhamdulillah, insya-Allah.”

According to Mohd Syahir, the meeting took place with Hadi Awang’s blessings and was described as a “casual” encounter following Muhyiddin’s return from overseas. He declined to confirm whether it was linked to speculation that Dr Samsuri might replace Muhyiddin as PN chairman.

Nevertheless, the timing of the photo — just days before PAS is expected to hold discussions on PN’s leadership following Muhyiddin’s resignation — makes its political signalling hard to ignore.

PAS has reportedly proposed two names to replace Muhyiddin: Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man and Dr Samsuri, while Bersatu’s Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin has also been floated as a potential contender.

5) Replacing Muhyiddin with Dr Sam Is Going in Circles

Yet when I look at that photograph, I feel an unmistakable sense of déjà vu.

Muhyiddin and Dr Samsuri give off the same energy.

If Perikatan replaces Muhyiddin with Dr Samsuri, it risks repeating the very mistake that has paralysed it for years. Dr Samsuri may well offer Perikatan the same calmness, the same gentlemanly restraint, and ultimately, the same strategic inertia.

That is precisely what frustrated both PAS and Bersatu about Muhyiddin in the first place — to the point that they have been trying, quietly and not so quietly, to ease him out for years.

Replacing Muhyiddin with Dr Samsuri may simply condemn Perikatan to another cycle of stagnation, followed by another prolonged and awkward attempt to remove a leader who appears decent and well-meaning, but lacks the ruthlessness and fire needed to win.

Once on top, Perikatan might find it just as difficult to remove Dr Sam as it did Muhyiddin, because like Muhyiddin, Dr Sam also has a nice guy vibe. Nobody likes to be the one to remove a nice guy, because it makes you look like a nasty guy, even if the nice guy deserves to be removed, because he is a weak guy. This problem of removing a nice guy, might be why it has taken Perikatan so long to remove Muhyiddin, despite the fact that he has provided ineffective leadership for years. 

6) Insanity, the Titanic, and the Violin

Einstein famously defined insanity as doing the same thing repeatedly while expecting a different result.

Replacing Muhyiddin with Dr Samsuri fits that definition perfectly.

Perhaps, after Perikatan has won power, stabilised governance, and secured broad public approval, someone like Dr Samsuri could serve as a capable legacy carrier.

But to put him in charge now — when Perikatan must charge uphill, under siege, against a well-entrenched Pakatan Harapan — is like appointing the bandleader of the Titanic as captain. 

All that is going to happen is that the Dr Sam, like Muhyiddin, will be playing the violin calmly, as the titanic called Perikatan continues to sink to the bottom of the ocean.

A 100% Malay-Bumiputera Government Isn’t the End for Non-Malays – It’s the End of the Biggest Lie in Malaysian History

There’s a lot of buzz in town about the possibility of DAP pulling its support from the government. 

In this hypothetical scenario, PKR might join forces with UMNO, Bersatu, and PAS to form a 100% Malay-Bumiputera government.

Now, what about the ultra-Malay segments who might celebrate this as a victory? 

It’s an early, premature celebration by shallow-minded folks who don’t understand the laws of nature, politics, and human behavior. 

On the surface, it looks like a unified 100% Malay-Bumiputera government.

But dig deeper, and it’s actually Malay political parties restricting and counterbalancing each other’s growth. 

What does that mean? If they unite, they’re forced to maintain the status quo, benefiting the current incumbents but stifling expansion.

Let’s break down the numbers: PAS holds 43 seats, UMNO 26, Bersatu 31, and PKR 31, totaling 131 seats. But only about 100 of those are truly secure (from UMNO, Bersatu, and PAS). 

Most of PKR’s seats are in urban mixed areas that rely on DAP’s core supporter base—they might not hold all of them. 

Even if all these parties combine, they might not dethrone DAP, not because DAP is invincible, but because its urban majority seats like Bukit Bintang, Cheras, and Kepong are rock-solid. 

Even if all Bumiputera votes consolidate, they couldn’t overtake DAP in those areas.

As the Chinese proverb goes: “One mountain can have only one tiger.” 

On the surface, it’s a 100% Bumiputera government, but behind the scenes, you’re putting tigers like Anwar, Mahathir, Muhyiddin, Hadi, and Zahid in the same arena. 

It’s only a matter of time before they start clashing and eliminating each other. 

Some might ask what I mean by Malay parties restricting one another?

If the status quo remains unchallenged, it prevents UMNO from returning to its former glory—they’ll be stuck at 26 seats.

It halts PAS’s “green wave,” leaving them at 43 seats. 

This creates a stalemate and stagnation for all Malay-Bumiputera parties. How can they grow when they can’t contest against each other?

PAS also can’t push its Islamic agenda to turn the country into an Islamic state. It’s a myth that only non-Malays oppose this—the UMNO, PKR, and Bersatu Malays have different DNA, psychology, and worldviews from PAS. 

If UMNO wanted an Islamic state, they could have done it during their heyday with a two-thirds majority as Malaysia’s largest undisputed party.

What PAS fails to understand is that not all Malays share their religious views on politics and administration.

Sooner or later, these parties will try to dominate one another. Each will plot to become the No. 1 Malay party. 

If Hamzah and Muhyiddin can fight within the same party, why is it abnormal for rival parties to scheme for ultimate dominance?

For stability, they’ll need the 56 MPs from Borneo. If they abandon this block, it’s risky—the 56 could align with DAP’s solid 40 seats and Amanah’s 8 to form a new government anytime. 

With 56 from Borneo versus PAS’s 43, Bersatu’s 31, PKR’s 31, and UMNO’s 26, Borneo becomes the kingmaker in this coalition. The moderates and progressives will call the shots.

This is what true Bumiputera check-and-balance looks like: parties counter-influencing and restricting each other. 

PAS won’t be able to ban alcohol, not because of DAP or non-Malay MPs, but because the Borneo Bumiputera won’t allow it—doing so would collapse GPS in Sarawak. That’s why a PAS candidate in Sabah even lodged a report denying plans to ban alcohol.

Not only is this their ceiling since they can’t contest each other, but it also limits their growth and puts everything in stalemate.

Yet UMNO won’t stay silent for long—their entire DNA is rooted in feudal elitism and a dominance mindset. They can’t accept being the smallest Malay party at just 26 seats.

And since non-Bumiputera are out of the government, those seats are no longer a conflict of interest. Non-Bumiputera will no longer be the election scapegoat, punching bag, or weaponized issue.

By then, it’ll be Bumiputera versus Bumiputera, outcompeting each other: left vs. right, conservative vs. progressive, religion-ahead-of-race vs. race-ahead-of-religion, B40 vs. M40 and T20, and the list goes on.

It’ll still be Bumiputera vs. Bumiputera, driven by the laws of human nature, politics, greed, dominance, power, and money.

As for PKR? There’s nothing to celebrate. Their 31 mixed urban seats are the most fragile and vulnerable in this combo, likely making them the smallest party in the Bumiputera coalition. 

It’ll also mark the end of any future prime minister from PKR. With non-Bumiputera out of the equation, whoever rises to the top in each Bumiputera party automatically wins big.

So, each party will see fierce internal killings to climb the ladder—just like UMNO in its glory days, or what’s happening in Bersatu now.

Everyone fighting for positions, candidacies, and more, because internal victory means a shot at PM. It’ll create a Game of Thrones among the Bumiputera parties.

Which party controls which GLCs and their multi-billion-ringgit empires

Who gets the powerful minister portfolios
who heads the government agencies, statutory bodies, and regulators

All the way down to who becomes Ketua Kampung, penghulu, JKKK chairs, and every small contract and perk that comes with it.

When the “enemy” (non-Malays) is removed from the equation, the knives will turn inward even faster—pure Bumiputera musical chairs with real money, real power, and real blood.

What do non-Bumiputera have to lose? We already have nothing to begin with, always relying on ourselves. Even having our own race in the cabinet changes little—we’re still blamed and used as punching bags by aspiring politicians and parties.

And Here’s the Biggest Silver Lining Most People Miss

When the non-Malays are completely out of the government, the real true colours of Malay politicians will finally be exposed – not to us, but to their own community.

For decades, the narrative has been drilled into the Malay heartland: “Melayu terancam! Islam terancam! The Chinese are the root of your poverty!” They were told the enemy is the non-Malays – that if only we remove the non-Malays, everything will be fair, just, and prosperous for the Malays.

But the moment a 100% Bumiputera government is formed, that entire lie collapses in plain sight.

The ordinary kampung folk, the B40 Malays, the PAS supporters, the Perikatan die-hards – they will finally see with their own eyes:

The rich and elite Malays will keep getting richer.

The poor Malays will stay poor, or get even poorer.

Government projects, contracts, GLCs, and billions in wealth will still flow to the same handful of elite Malay families, cronies, and political warlords – just like before.

Their own leaders will stop fighting for them. Why? Because there is no longer a “non-Malay enemy” to rally against. No more “Cina yang halang kita!” to shout from the stages. When the votes are already 100% locked in, what slogan is left? 

Sooner or later, the realisation will hit like a thunderbolt: “Rupa-rupanya selama ini kita dipergunakan sahaja. Kita dijadikan senjata untuk lawan orang bukan Melayu, supaya segelintir ahli politik Melayu boleh naik kuasa dan kaya raya untuk diri dan keluarga mereka sendiri.

Rupa-rupanya ini bukan perjuangan bangsa dan agama – ini perjuangan pangkat, jawatan, wang, dan kemewahan peribadi.”

Even the most hardcore PAS supporters will wake up: “Rupa-rupanya 100% kerajaan Melayu-Bumiputera pun hudud tak dapat, negara Islam pun tak jadi. Sebelum ini kita ingat orang bukan Melayu yang halang – rupanya bukan!”

That moment of mass awakening among the Malay grassroots will be the most powerful, most irreversible change of all. The spell will be broken forever.

And that, ironically, might be the greatest gift a DAP withdrawal could ever give to this country – forcing the Malay community to finally see their real oppressors have never been the non-Malays sitting in Putrajaya. 

The real oppressors have always been wearing the same songkok and speaking the same language as them.

So let them have their 100% Malay-Bumiputera Government if they want it so badly.

It won’t destroy the non-Malays. 

It will destroy the biggest lie they’ve been feeding their own people for seventy years.

The biggest membership.

The most prepared leaders.

No more whispered complaints about being sidelined.
No more dreams of sneaking back to Muafakat Nasional like an ex texting at 2 a.m.

This is leadership without disclaimers.

The dog has caught the car.
Now it must decide whether to drive—or be dragged.

governing.
Not preaching. Not posturing. Not praying for opponents to fall.

Leading.

Budgets. Policies. Accountability. Decisions that cannot be footnoted with verses when they go wrong.

This is no longer about who controls PN.

A Bersatu Menteri Besar.
PAS sidelined.
Trust eroded.
Smiles that didn’t reach the eyes.

it is their own alliance that is losing its footing.

Trigger a leadership vacuum.

No blood. No bruises. No public humiliation.

PAS now grips the steering wheel of PN with both hands.

Does PAS actually want to lead?

Mazlan Ali of Universiti Teknologi Malaysia said the dispute had become increasingly serious over the past year, citing tensions in Perlis and Negeri Sembilan.

“This serious dispute between PAS and Bersatu will lead to a direct split,” he told FMT.

Mazlan said PAS appears to be recalibrating its political strategy around former Bersatu deputy president Hamzah Zainudin and the Reset movement linked to him.

“I think there is a possibility that Reset will replace Bersatu as PAS’s main partner in PN,” he said, adding that Bersatu could eventually be sidelined ahead of the next general election.

Last week, PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang said the party was reassessing ties with Bersatu, citing several disagreements involving Negeri Sembilan, Perlis, Kedah and Kelantan.

Bersatu later responded by expressing regret over Hadi’s remarks, saying coalition matters should be resolved through PN’s Supreme Council.

Mazlan said PAS has emerged as the dominant force in PN because of its grassroots machinery and parliamentary strength.

“PAS is the big brother in PN,” he said.

He said Hadi’s decision to publicly criticise Bersatu instead of discussing the matter internally showed PAS was confident it could survive without Bersatu.

PAS also appears less interested in strengthening ties with PN’s non-Malay component parties, including Gerakan and Malaysian Indian People’s Party, said Mazlan.

“PAS is more comfortable with the Malay-Muslim narrative because it allows the party to maintain its power base in Malay-majority areas,” he said.

Mazlan said an alignment between PAS and Hamzah could see Muhyiddin Yassin marginalised.

He said Bersatu could then form a separate bloc with Gerakan and MIPP, contest independently, or seek cooperation with either Pakatan Harapan or Barisan Nasional.

Azmi Hassan of Akademi Nusantara also sees Hadi’s open criticism of Bersatu as a serious development.

“I think the end game for PAS is that they just want to get rid of Bersatu,” he said.

Azmi said PAS wants to open PN to smaller Malay-Muslim parties, while Bersatu opposes new membership out of concern that Hamzah could return through a different platform.

He also said PAS’s growing dominance in PN could create unease among non-Malay voters and component parties.

“I think Gerakan and MIPP know this,” he said.

Perpaduan tidak lahir secara spontan. Ia dibina melalui interaksi berterusan, sikap saling menghormati dan kesediaan untuk memahami perbezaan.

Memasuki tahun baharu, Lajnah Perpaduan Nasional menyeru seluruh masyarakat agar menolak politik kebencian dan memperkukuh budaya saling percaya.

A New Year, A Renewed Commitment to Unity

As we step into a new year, it is more than a change of date, it is an opportunity to renew our commitment to building stronger relationships within our diverse society.

The National Unity Committee views this new year as an important moment to strengthen unity among communities of different backgrounds, cultures, and beliefs.
Unity does not happen by chance. It is built through consistent engagement, mutual respect, and a willingness to understand one another.

Over the past year, the National Unity Committee has actively implemented grassroots initiatives such as Ziarah Mahabbah, joint activities with tai chi groups, multicultural cultural celebrations, community dialogues, and inclusive social programmes that bring people together beyond racial or religious lines. These efforts demonstrate that unity grows through genuine human connection and shared experiences.

The Chairperson of the National Unity Committee, Zarina binti Abd Rahman, emphasised that unity must be reflected in real actions. “Unity should never remain a slogan. It must be translated into our daily interactions, our presence within the community, and our willingness to share spaces with respect and sincerity,” she said.

As we welcome the new year, the National Unity Committee calls on all members of society to reject divisive narratives and instead nurture empathy, dialogue, and cooperation.

Let us begin with simple acts, kind words, respectful actions, and an open heart towards one another.

May this new year bring greater harmony, maturity, and unity, for the well-being of our communities and a more peaceful future for our nation.

National Unity Committee

Give Malaysia a chance for a new government

This 15th general election is an election to elect a new government. It is also to determine a future that we can all be proud of for Malaysia. 

All elections before 2018 were always about electing a stronger opposition. Barisan Nasional was always the only government we knew. Pakatan Harapan and all other previous opposition coalitions were supposedly the permanent opposition. 

Now, things have changed. This GE15 is a competition of three potential governments - Pakatan Harapan, Barisan Nasional, and Perikatan Nasional. 

Pakatan Harapan has a clear choice of Prime Minister in Dato’ Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

BN has named Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob but most likely would see UMNO President Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi as Prime Minister should it win a majority. PN offers Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin who has been tainted as leader of a “kerajaan gagal” (failed government) during Covid-19 pandemic. 

Pakatan Harapan also has a talent pool of multiracial and nationally known leaders who are sincere, competent and visionary. Both BN and PN have less competent leaders.  

All opinion polls published in the past few days placed Pakatan Harapan at the top with between 80 and 95 parliamentary seats nationally, and with a significant number of other seats in the “too-close-to-call” category, which will likely add to Pakatan Harapan’s column in the event that voter turnout exceeds 80%. 

I am putting Pakatan Harapan’s seat count at 100 and above out of the total 222 seats. If turnout is very high across the nation, Pakatan Harapan may have a chance to reach 112 or very close to the number on its own. 

PN, in particular PAS, is likely to make gains in Perlis and the seats east of the Banjaran Titiwangsa, at the expense of BN.  

There is now a distinct possibility that BN might end up at number 3 in terms of seat count in the Peninsula, after Pakatan Harapan and PN.  

It is not difficult to explain this logic: if BN  suffers a massive bleeding of its base vote, even if those votes go to PN in the Peninsula’s west coast, such a shift would benefit Pakatan Harapan, which will further deplete the number of seats BN would win. Whereas in Perlis and the east coast, BN  may suffer more losses due to the sheer hatred among Malay voters against Zahid Hamidi.

The greatest irony of the UMNO-led “Malay unity” coalition is that all the parties - UMNO, Bersatu and PAS were always suspicious of each other. UMNO had tried to eat up Bersatu for the past two years, successfully  kicking out Prime Minister Muhyiddin out of office. PAS keeps on changing partners, yesterday with UMNO, today with Bersatu, tomorrow, who knows.  

I believe PAS will likely ditch Bersatu after GE15 if PN fails to win power or form a coalition government with other parties. 

An important lesson for all: a sustainable governing coalition in Malaysia has to be one that is accepted and embraced by all ethnic groups and able to win some seats or have partners in Sabah and Sarawak. This is the Pakatan Harapan formula. It represents the broadest Malaysian spectrum possible. 

All other forces such as BN and PN that try to divide Malaysia would never win enough votes from middle ground Malaysians who are increasingly more mature and less susceptible to racial and religious incitements. 

I hope Pakatan Harapan will win an outright 111 seats tomorrow, and be given the chance to govern well for the next five years to prove that Malaysia can prosper without too much racial and religious prejudices.   

A Pakatan Harapan government that cares will help many families live a much better economic life and help steer the nation forward during turbulent times in the global economy. We need a dynamic yet humane economy for all.  

A Pakatan Harapan government will sustain a democracy with institutions that have integrity. Enough of corruption and cronyism. 

A Pakatan Harapan government will see Malaysians believing in the idea that Malaysia can be a nation that is filled with hope, potentials and possibilities. 

The votes you cast tomorrow will change the nation for the better, and we shall remember the day as the beginning of a new era which hopefully will last for years if not decades. 

Let's give this nation a chance for rebuilding under the leadership of Dato' Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

Let's give Malaysia a chance.

However, PMX called the people who wishes for the quota system to be abolished an extremist. As the PM of Malaysia, and an advocate for equity and equality, this is uncalled for.

The abolition of the quota system has been long overdue. Students no longer having equal rights to education, rejecting non-bumiputeras just because academic and curricular merits is no longer the main consideration of accepting a student. To ensure equal rights to education, the quota system must be abolished and replaced with the meritocracy system. Ini diduga sebagai akar penembakan tiga anggota kepolisian oleh dua prajurit TNI yang terjadi di Kampung Karang Manik, Senin 17 Maret 2025 lalu.

Kapendam menyampaikan, setoran dan bagi-bagi uang tersebut merupakan komitmen antara kepolisian dan militer di Negara Batin. Komitmen itu berupa ‘pengamanan’ bisnis perjudian sabung ayam di Kampung Karang Manik tersebut. Keterangan itu diperoleh dari hasil pemeriksaan internal terhadap Kopka Basarsyah dan Peltu Lubis, pemilik lokasi perjudian sabung ayam. Kedua aggota TNI yang sudah mengakui dan menyerahkan diri sebagai pelaku penembakan yang menewaskan tiga personel Polri.

Sementara itu, Kepolisian Daerah (Polda) Lampung meminta pihak yang menyebarkan isu ada setoran diterima anggota dari aktivitas judi sabung ayam di Kabupaten Way Kanan menunjukkan bukti. Bila benar terbukti, maka anggota yang bersalah akan diproses. 

‘’Jadi isunya kan disebutkan baik Koramil, maupun Polsek di sana menerima setoran, kalau memang iya langsung ditindaklanjuti dan saya yakin dari TNI juga akan melakukan penindakan kalau memang benar,’’ kata Kapolda Lampung Irjen Pol Helmy Santika dalam keterangannya, di Provinsi Lampung, Sabtu.

Menurutnya, isu yang beredar bahwa tragedi penembakan dipicu masalah setoran adalah asumsi tak mendasar. Ia mengatakan, kalaupun memang ada setoran, itu tetap tidak menghilangkan fakta penembakan yang menyebabkan tiga orang meninggal dunia.

Perpecahan antara Parti Islam Se-Malaysia (PAS) dan Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (BERSATU) dalam gabungan Perikatan Nasional (PN) kelihatan "semakin ketara". Hal ini  dinyatakan oleh felo Geostrategis dan Felo Kanan Akademi Penyelidikan Strategik Nusantara (NASR), Profesor Dr. Azmi Hassan, selepas Naib Presiden PAS, Datuk Mohd Amar Abdullah, mengaburkan gambar sepanduk PN yang digantung di lokasi ceramah baru-baru ini.

Memetik laporan Free Malaysia Today (FMT), Azmi Hassan berkata, hubungan tegang antara dua komponen PN ini mula kelihatan semasa kempen pilihan raya kecil Kuala Kubu Baharu dua bulan lalu. 

"Apa yang cuba ditunjukkan oleh PAS ialah mereka boleh bergerak sendirian tanpa Bersatu. Ini benar terutamanya di kawasan seperti Sungai Bakap dan lain-lain di mana pengundi Melayu membentuk lebih 60% hingga 70% daripada jumlah pengundi," katanya kepada FMT. 

Azmi menambah, gambar yang dimuat naik oleh Amar juga menguatkan spekulasi bahawa PAS mungkin terlibat dalam "perbincangan" untuk bekerjasama dengan kerajaan perpaduan pimpinan Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim. 

Minggu lalu, jurucakap kerajaan perpaduan Fahmi Fadzil enggan mengulas mengenai spekulasi PAS menyertai gabungan perpaduan, manakala beberapa pemimpin PAS menafikan dakwaan tersebut. Walau bagaimanapun, Azmi berpendapat perbincangan tersebut mungkin lebih kepada usaha menjalinkan hubungan dengan Putrajaya. 

"Saya rasa PAS cuba untuk lebih mesra dengan kerajaan persekutuan, bukan khusus dengan Pakatan Harapan atau UMNO," katanya lagi. 

Amar, yang juga Speaker Dewan Undangan Negeri Kelantan, pada 24 Jun lalu memuat naik beberapa gambar dirinya berucap dalam ceramah semasa kempen pilihan raya kecil Sungai Bakap. Enam daripada gambar tersebut kelihatan mengaburkan sepanduk PN. 

Namun, Pensyarah Kanan di Pusat Pengajian Sains Kemasyarakatan, Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) Dr Azmil Mohd Tayeb menegaskan untuk tidak membuat kesimpulan terburu-buru mengenai perkara ini. 

"Saya tidak akan terlalu menekankan perkara ini. Kemungkinan PAS menyertai kerajaan Madani adalah tipis selagi DAP berada dalam kerajaan," katanya.

Oleh: Roslinda Hashim 

PADANG TERAP - Menteri Besar Kedah, Dato’ Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor mengajak akar umbi UMNO khususnya golongan muda supaya bersama PAS dan Perikatan Nasional (PN) membina landskap politik baharu bagi memperkukuhkan kuasa Islam dan Melayu di negara ini.

Ketua Pengarah Pilihan Raya PAS Pusat itu berkata, Pilihan Raya Umum ke-16 (PRU16) perlu dijadikan medan untuk memastikan tampuk pemerintahan negara terus diterajui orang Islam Melayu demi menjamin kestabilan serta keharmonian masyarakat pelbagai kaum.

“Rakan-rakan dalam UMNO, marilah bersama kami. Kita nak kuatkan orang Melayu, pegang kuasa bersungguh-sungguh. Negara ini siasah politiknya mesti dipegang dan dikawal oleh orang Islam Melayu.

“Bila Melayu dan Islam kuat, bangsa lain juga akan hidup selamat, bebas dan harmoni di negara ini,” katanya ketika berucap pada majlis Pelancaran Jentera Pilihan Raya PAS Kawasan Padang Terap, pada Rabu.

Menurut beliau, PAS tidak pernah melupakan detik kerjasama bersama UMNO menerusi Muafakat Nasional (MN) yang disifatkan berjaya menyatukan orang Melayu dan Islam sehingga mewujudkan semangat baharu kalangan rakyat di peringkat akar umbi.

“Kita dengan UMNO pernah berkawan bawah Muafakat Nasional, kita tak pernah lupa saat manis di peringkat akar umbi.

“Kita masih ingat bagaimana orang kampung, ahli UMNO dan PAS ketika itu duduk bersama. Saya yakin ahli UMNO masih terasa seronoknya berkawan dengan PAS, masa itu kutip derma guna tin milo semasa ceramah.

“Mereka belajar berjuang dalam politik dengan pengorbanan, bukan untuk cari habuan atau nikmat,” katanya.

Bagaimanapun, Sanusi tegaskan, PAS dan UMNO bukan lagi rakan politik pada masa kini selepas UMNO mengambil keputusan bekerjasama dengan DAP dan PKR bagi membentuk Kerajaan Perpaduan.

Menurutnya, tindakan itu berlaku selepas Presiden UMNO, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi menarik parti tersebut keluar daripada Muafakat Nasional.

“Kerana kepentingan peribadi untuk selamatkan diri daripada kes mahkamah, UMNO dibawa berpakat dengan DAP dan PKR. Mereka mula cari habuan, ramai pemimpin yang kalah dalam pilihan raya dilantik memegang jawatan lembaga pengarah di sana sini tanpa mengambil kira kelayakan atau pengalaman,” ujarnya.

Pengerusi PN Kedah itu berkata, UMNO pernah meminda perlembagaan parti itu dengan memasukkan perjuangan Islam, selepas menjalinkan kerjasama dengan PAS menerusi Muafakat Nasional.

Namun katanya, parti itu kini lebih memberi tumpuan kepada usaha mendapatkan semula kuasa politik termasuk menyerang pentadbiran Kerajaan Negeri Kedah.

“Mereka nak ambil alih kuasa di sini. Kalau nak lawan kita, buatlah kerja elok-elok, tetapi hakikatnya kita buat lebih baik daripada ketika mereka memerintah dahulu,” katanya.

POIN UTAMA PASAL 412 KUHP BARU:
Ancaman Pidana: Pelaku kumpul kebo dapat diancam pidana penjara paling lama 6 bulan atau denda kategori II (maksimal Rp10 juta).
Siapa yang Berhak Mengadu?: Karena bersifat delik aduan, polisi hanya bisa bertindak jika ada laporan dari pihak keluarga inti, yaitu:
Suami atau Istri (bagi pelaku yang sudah terikat perkawinan).
Orang Tua atau Anak (bagi pelaku yang tidak terikat perkawinan).
Warga Tidak Bisa Melapor: Tetangga, warga sekitar, atau organisasi masyarakat tidak memiliki kedudukan hukum (legal standing) untuk melaporkan pasal ini. Melaporkan orang lain tanpa hubungan kekeluargaan justru berisiko terkena pasal pencemaran nama baik.
Pengecualian Ketertiban Umum: Warga hanya bisa melapor jika pasangan tersebut mengganggu ketertiban umum (seperti kebisingan atau pesta pora), namun bukan atas dasar pasal perzinaan atau kumpul kebo itu sendiri.

Kisah Warga Kemalingan Motor : Seminggu Setelah Laporan, Polisi Tak Datang ke TKP, Baru Muncul Setelah Beritanya Viral di TV

----------------------------------------------------------------------

Kisah ini terjadi di Kebayoran Baru, Jakarta Selatan.

Seorang warga, yang kebetulan anggota TNI, yakni Sertu Mualimin kehilangan sepeda motor di rumahnya, Jalan Dasa IV, Kebayoran Baru, Jaksel pada 17 Agustus 2025.

Karena kesal polisi tak bergerak, ia membuat sayembara sendiri.

Siapa yang menemukan motor iu, dapat hadiah.

Tatu, sang istri, mengatakan pihak kepolisian tak cepat bergerak meski sudah ada laporan.

Tatu menyoroti polisi yang tak kunjung melakukan olah TKP di rumahnya untuk mengambil sidik jari pelaku di pagar rumahnya. 

Padahal, orang rumah sudah bela-belain untuk mensterilkan TKP.

“Sidik jari pasti kan masih ada orang-orang, belum ada yang megang pas hari itu. Tapi belum ada (polisi) sampai sekarang ke sini,” kata dia, dikutip dari Kompas-com, Selasa (26/8/2025). 

Empat hari usai kejadian, Tatu sempat kedatangan dua wartawan media televisi swasta. 

Tatu mengira itu adalah penyidik dari Polres Jakarta Selatan. 

Setelah kejadian itu ditayangkan di televisi, eh, tim kepolisian baru menghubungi Mualimin untuk datang ke Mapolres Jakarta Selatan. 

“Udah viral di TV, baru dia gerak. kemarin suami saya dapat kabar dari Polres, ada panggilan. Kemarin ke mana saja? Masa sudah seminggu belum olah TKP,” keluh Tatu. 

Terpisah, Kasi Humas Polres Jakarta Selatan, Kompol Murodih, menyebutkan bahwa kasus pencurian motor tersebut sedang dalam penyelidikan oleh Unit Reserse Kriminal. 

“Untuk ini (laporan curanmor) masih kami lidik,” kata Murodih saat dikonfirmasi, Senin.

Baiknya anggaran Polri rp 100 triliun dihapus.
Polisi sdh tidak melayani, melindungi, dan mengayomi masyarakat.
Malu makan gaji buta

Travel memory: Good morning, virtual adventurers! Today is Friday, May 8, 2026, and I’m really looking forward to taking you on a spectacular journey into the heart of Portuguese history. Our virtual adventure takes us to one of Lisbon’s most famous landmarks—the Tower of Belém, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its majestic beauty, fascinating legends, and historical significance. Get ready for an immersive exploration of this architectural masterpiece, which once served as Portugal’s gateway to the world. Let’s dive in and uncover the secrets behind this mythical tower, which has stood steadfast on the banks of the Tagus for centuries!

A Symbol of Power and the Spirit of Discovery - Built between 1514 and 1519 under King Manuel I, the Tower of Belém was originally intended as a coastal fortification to protect Lisbon from naval attacks. However, it became far more than just a military structure. Richly decorated with motifs in the Manueline style—including twisted ropes, Crosses of the Order of Christ, and armillary spheres—the tower embodied Portugal’s maritime supremacy during the Age of Discovery. Strategically located at the river’s mouth, the Torre de Belém witnessed fleets full of explorers, spices, and treasures setting sail for distant lands—and welcomed them back as symbols of Portugal’s global reach. When you imagine its observation decks, reminiscent of ship decks, and the ornate decorations inspired by exotic cultures, it quickly becomes clear how the tower visually reflects the spirit of adventure that defined this era.

The Rhinoceros Sculpture: A Story of Cultural Fusion - Among the many stories engraved in the stone of this monument, one particularly fascinating detail awaits discovery—a rhinoceros carved into the north facade. This sculpture depicts a real rhinoceros that was gifted to King Manuel I by an Indian ruler in 1515. Although the rhinoceros was tragically lost at sea on its way to Rome, it left an indelible legacy. It inspired Albrecht Dürer’s famous drawings and found eternal life in the carvings of the Torre de Belém. This seemingly small detail reveals a broader truth about Portugal’s maritime adventures: these voyages were not merely about claiming land; they also brought with them animals, ideas, and cultural exchange that forever altered the fabric of Europe.

Myths Surrounding the Tagus and the Tower - A captivating legend surrounding the Torre de Belém claims that it was originally built in the middle of the Tagus but was moved closer to the shore after the devastating earthquake of 1755. In reality, the truth lies in the subtle shifts of the coastline over the centuries. The tower was built on a small island near the coast, which gradually expanded and connected the structure to the mainland. Even though debunking this myth does not diminish its charm, the image of a tower rising from the water contributes to its mystical appeal—a lasting symbol of how Portugal once ruled the vast oceans.

The Tower’s Dark Chapters - Aside from its romantic and adventurous past, the tower also harbors darker stories. In its later years, the Torre de Belém served as a prison, particularly under the reign of King Miguel I in the 19th century. Its cold chambers—originally intended for storing weapons—were repurposed to imprison political opponents and dissidents. These haunting episodes remind us that even places of grandeur have their dark sides. The contrasting layers of light and darkness in the tower’s history make it all the more fascinating—a reflection of Portugal’s struggles and triumphs over time.

An Architectural Journey Through Time - The Torre de Belém embodies centuries of architectural evolution. Under the architect Francisco de Arruda, influences from Moorish art were integrated, evident in the geometric patterns, ribbed domes, and elegant arcades that adorn its structure. Later, in the 19th century, romantic embellishments accentuated its Manueline style, transforming the fortress into a feast for the eyes. As you admire the intricate details, you’ll notice how the tower serves as a bridge between eras, combining defensive purpose with breathtaking craftsmanship—a true architectural time capsule.

One of the Seven Wonders of Portugal - It comes as no surprise that the Torre de Belém was named “One of the Seven Wonders of Portugal” in 2007. Tourists flock here not only for its historical significance but also for the breathtaking panoramic view it offers over the Tagus River. Thousands climb to its summit every year to marvel at a landmark that stands as both a physical and symbolic gateway to Portugal’s glorious past.

A Living Time Capsule - The Torre de Belém defies the passage of time; its walls preserve the essence of Portuguese identity. From its role in the Age of Discovery, through its time as a prison, to its designation as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the tower embodies courage, innovation, and the spirit of discovery. When you step inside, it feels as though you’re entering another world—a world where the echoes of distant voyages mingle with the whispers of those who once walked its corridors.

Your Gateway to History - The Torre de Belém is not just a building—it is a testament to Portugal’s boldness, creativity, and resilience. Whether you are drawn to its historical significance, its architectural beauty, or the legends that surround it, you are guaranteed to leave feeling inspired. 

Thank you so much for joining me on today’s virtual adventure! Tomorrow we’ll embark on a new journey to discover another treasure of our shared human history. Until then, I wish you a wonderful day. Best regards, Freddy Kalder

Souvenir de voyage : Bonjour, aventuriers virtuels ! Nous sommes aujourd’hui vendredi 8 mai 2026, et j’ai vraiment hâte de vous emmener dans un voyage spectaculaire au cœur de l’histoire du Portugal. Notre aventure virtuelle nous conduit vers l’un des monuments les plus célèbres de Lisbonne : la Tour de Belém, classée au patrimoine mondial de l’UNESCO, réputée pour sa beauté majestueuse, ses légendes fascinantes et son importance historique. Préparez-vous à une exploration immersive de ce chef-d’œuvre architectural, qui servait autrefois de porte d’entrée du Portugal sur le monde. Plongeons-nous dans cette tour mythique et découvrons ses secrets, qui se dresse fièrement sur les rives du Tage depuis des siècles !

Un symbole de puissance et de l'esprit de découverte - Construite entre 1514 et 1519 sous le règne du roi Manuel Ier, la tour de Belém était à l'origine destinée à servir de fortification côtière pour protéger Lisbonne des attaques navales. Cependant, elle est devenue bien plus qu'une simple structure militaire. Richement décorée de motifs de style manuélin — notamment des cordes torsadées, des croix de l’Ordre du Christ et des sphères armillaires —, la tour incarnait la suprématie maritime du Portugal à l’époque des grandes découvertes. Stratégiquement située à l’embouchure du fleuve, la Torre de Belém a vu des flottes chargées d’explorateurs, d’épices et de trésors mettre le cap vers des contrées lointaines — et les a accueillies à leur retour comme symboles de l’influence mondiale du Portugal. Lorsque l’on imagine ses ponts d’observation, qui rappellent ceux des navires, et ses décorations somptueuses inspirées de cultures exotiques, on comprend rapidement à quel point la tour reflète visuellement l’esprit d’aventure qui a défini cette époque.

La sculpture du rhinocéros : une histoire de fusion culturelle - Parmi les nombreuses histoires gravées dans la pierre de ce monument, un détail particulièrement fascinant attend d’être découvert : un rhinocéros sculpté sur la façade nord. Cette sculpture représente un véritable rhinocéros offert au roi Manuel Ier par un souverain indien en 1515. Bien que le rhinocéros ait tragiquement péri en mer alors qu’il était en route pour Rome, il a laissé un héritage indélébile. Il a inspiré les célèbres dessins d’Albrecht Dürer et a trouvé une vie éternelle dans les sculptures de la Torre de Belém. Ce détail en apparence insignifiant révèle une vérité plus large sur les aventures maritimes du Portugal : ces voyages ne visaient pas seulement à revendiquer des terres ; ils ont également apporté avec eux des animaux, des idées et des échanges culturels qui ont bouleversé à jamais le tissu de l’Europe.

Mythes entourant le Tage et la tour - Une légende captivante entourant la Torre de Belém prétend qu’elle fut à l’origine construite au milieu du Tage, mais qu’elle fut déplacée plus près du rivage après le tremblement de terre dévastateur de 1755. En réalité, la vérité réside dans les subtils changements du littoral au fil des siècles. La tour a été construite sur une petite île près de la côte, qui s’est progressivement étendue et a relié la structure au continent. Même si le fait de démystifier ce mythe n’enlève rien à son charme, l’image d’une tour s’élevant de l’eau contribue à son attrait mystique — un symbole durable de la façon dont le Portugal régnait autrefois sur les vastes océans.

Les chapitres sombres de la tour - Outre son passé romantique et aventureux, la tour recèle également des histoires plus sombres. Au cours de ses dernières années, la Torre de Belém a servi de prison, en particulier sous le règne du roi Miguel Ier au XIXe siècle. Ses chambres froides — initialement destinées au stockage des armes — ont été réaffectées pour emprisonner les opposants politiques et les dissidents. Ces épisodes obsédants nous rappellent que même les lieux de grandeur ont leurs côtés sombres. Les contrastes entre lumière et obscurité qui marquent l’histoire de la tour la rendent d’autant plus fascinante : elle est le reflet des luttes et des triomphes du Portugal au fil du temps.

Un voyage architectural à travers le temps - La Torre de Belém incarne des siècles d’évolution architecturale. Sous la direction de l’architecte Francisco de Arruda, des influences de l’art mauresque ont été intégrées, comme en témoignent les motifs géométriques, les dômes nervurés et les élégantes arcades qui ornent sa structure. Plus tard, au XIXe siècle, des ornements romantiques ont accentué son style manuélin, transformant la forteresse en un véritable régal pour les yeux. En admirant les détails complexes, vous remarquerez comment la tour sert de pont entre les époques, alliant fonction défensive et savoir-faire artisanal époustouflant : une véritable capsule temporelle architecturale.

L'une des sept merveilles du Portugal - Il n'est pas surprenant que la Torre de Belém ait été désignée « l'une des sept merveilles du Portugal » en 2007. Les touristes s'y pressent non seulement pour son importance historique, mais aussi pour la vue panoramique à couper le souffle qu'elle offre sur le Tage. Des milliers de personnes gravissent son sommet chaque année pour s'émerveiller devant un monument qui se dresse comme une porte d'entrée à la fois physique et symbolique vers le glorieux passé du Portugal.

Une capsule temporelle vivante – La Torre de Belém défie le temps ; ses murs préservent l’essence de l’identité portugaise. De son rôle à l’époque des grandes découvertes, en passant par son utilisation comme prison, jusqu’à son inscription au patrimoine mondial de l’UNESCO, la tour incarne le courage, l’innovation et l’esprit de découverte. Lorsque vous y pénétrez, vous avez l’impression d’entrer dans un autre monde — un monde où les échos de voyages lointains se mêlent aux murmures de ceux qui ont autrefois arpenté ses couloirs.

Votre porte d’entrée vers l’histoire - La Torre de Belém n’est pas seulement un bâtiment — c’est un témoignage de l’audace, de la créativité et de la résilience du Portugal. Que vous soyez attiré par son importance historique, sa beauté architecturale ou les légendes qui l'entourent, vous repartirez à coup sûr inspiré.

Merci beaucoup de m'avoir accompagné dans cette aventure virtuelle d'aujourd'hui ! Demain, nous embarquerons pour un nouveau voyage à la découverte d'un autre trésor de notre histoire humaine commune. D'ici là, je vous souhaite une merveilleuse journée. Cordialement, Freddy Kalder

Ricordo di viaggio: Buongiorno, avventurieri virtuali! Oggi è venerdì 8 maggio 2026 e non vedo l’ora di accompagnarvi in un viaggio spettacolare nel cuore della storia portoghese. La nostra avventura virtuale ci porta in uno dei monumenti più famosi di Lisbona: la Torre di Belém, patrimonio mondiale dell’UNESCO, nota per la sua maestosa bellezza, le affascinanti leggende e il suo significato storico. Preparatevi a un'esplorazione immersiva di questo capolavoro architettonico, che un tempo fungeva da porta d'accesso del Portogallo al mondo. Immergiamoci e scopriamo i segreti che si celano dietro questa torre mitica, che da secoli si erge impassibile sulle rive del Tago!

Un simbolo di potere e dello spirito di scoperta - Costruita tra il 1514 e il 1519 sotto il re Manuele I, la Torre di Belém era originariamente concepita come fortificazione costiera per proteggere Lisbona dagli attacchi navali. Tuttavia, divenne molto più di una semplice struttura militare. Riccamente decorata con motivi in stile manuelino — tra cui corde intrecciate, croci dell’Ordine di Cristo e sfere armillari — la torre incarnava la supremazia marittima del Portogallo durante l’Era delle Scoperte. Situata strategicamente alla foce del fiume, la Torre di Belém ha visto flotte piene di esploratori, spezie e tesori salpare verso terre lontane — e le ha accolte al ritorno come simboli della portata globale del Portogallo. Se si immaginano i suoi ponti di osservazione, che ricordano i ponti delle navi, e le decorazioni ornate ispirate a culture esotiche, diventa subito chiaro come la torre rifletta visivamente lo spirito di avventura che ha caratterizzato quell’epoca.

La scultura del rinoceronte: una storia di fusione culturale - Tra le tante storie incise nella pietra di questo monumento, un dettaglio particolarmente affascinante attende di essere scoperto: un rinoceronte scolpito sulla facciata nord. Questa scultura raffigura un rinoceronte reale che fu donato al re Manuele I da un sovrano indiano nel 1515. Sebbene il rinoceronte andò tragicamente perduto in mare durante il viaggio verso Roma, lasciò un'eredità indelebile. Ispirò i famosi disegni di Albrecht Dürer e trovò vita eterna nelle sculture della Torre di Belém. Questo dettaglio apparentemente piccolo rivela una verità più ampia sulle avventure marittime del Portogallo: questi viaggi non miravano solo a rivendicare territori, ma portarono con sé anche animali, idee e scambi culturali che hanno cambiato per sempre il tessuto dell’Europa.

Miti sul Tago e sulla Torre - Un’affascinante leggenda sulla Torre di Belém sostiene che fosse stata originariamente costruita in mezzo al Tago, ma che sia stata spostata più vicino alla riva dopo il devastante terremoto del 1755. In realtà, la verità risiede nei sottili cambiamenti della linea costiera nel corso dei secoli. La torre fu costruita su una piccola isola vicino alla costa, che si espanse gradualmente e collegò la struttura alla terraferma. Anche se sfatare questo mito non ne diminuisce il fascino, l’immagine di una torre che sorge dall’acqua contribuisce al suo fascino mistico: un simbolo duraturo di come il Portogallo un tempo dominasse i vasti oceani.

I capitoli oscuri della Torre - Oltre al suo passato romantico e avventuroso, la torre custodisce anche storie più cupe. Negli ultimi anni, la Torre di Belém fu utilizzata come prigione, in particolare sotto il regno di re Miguel I nel XIX secolo. Le sue fredde celle, originariamente destinate al deposito delle armi, furono riadattate per imprigionare oppositori politici e dissidenti. Questi episodi inquietanti ci ricordano che anche i luoghi maestosi hanno i loro lati oscuri. I contrasti tra luce e oscurità nella storia della torre la rendono ancora più affascinante: un riflesso delle lotte e dei trionfi del Portogallo nel corso del tempo.

Un viaggio architettonico nel tempo - La Torre di Belém incarna secoli di evoluzione architettonica. Sotto la guida dell'architetto Francisco de Arruda, furono integrate influenze dell'arte moresca, evidenti nei motivi geometrici, nelle cupole a costoloni e negli eleganti portici che adornano la sua struttura. Più tardi, nel XIX secolo, abbellimenti romantici ne accentuarono lo stile manuelino, trasformando la fortezza in una festa per gli occhi. Ammirando i dettagli intricati, noterete come la torre funga da ponte tra le epoche, combinando lo scopo difensivo con un'artigianalità mozzafiato: una vera e propria capsula del tempo architettonica.

Una delle sette meraviglie del Portogallo - Non sorprende che la Torre di Belém sia stata nominata “Una delle sette meraviglie del Portogallo” nel 2007. I turisti accorrono qui non solo per il suo significato storico, ma anche per la vista panoramica mozzafiato che offre sul fiume Tago. Migliaia di persone salgono sulla sua cima ogni anno per ammirare un punto di riferimento che rappresenta una porta d’accesso sia fisica che simbolica al glorioso passato del Portogallo.

Una capsula del tempo vivente - La Torre di Belém sfida il passare del tempo; le sue mura conservano l’essenza dell’identità portoghese. Dal suo ruolo nell’Era delle Scoperte, passando per il periodo in cui fu utilizzata come prigione, fino alla sua designazione come Patrimonio Mondiale dell’UNESCO, la torre incarna il coraggio, l’innovazione e lo spirito di scoperta. Quando si entra, sembra di entrare in un altro mondo: un mondo in cui gli echi di viaggi lontani si mescolano ai sussurri di coloro che un tempo percorrevano i suoi corridoi.

La vostra porta d’accesso alla storia - La Torre di Belém non è solo un edificio: è una testimonianza dell’audacia, della creatività e della resilienza del Portogallo. Che siate attratti dal suo significato storico, dalla sua bellezza architettonica o dalle leggende che la circondano, ne uscirete sicuramente ispirati.

Grazie mille per avermi accompagnato nell'avventura virtuale di oggi! Domani intraprenderemo un nuovo viaggio alla scoperta di un altro tesoro della nostra storia umana comune. Nel frattempo, vi auguro una splendida giornata. Cordiali saluti, Freddy Kalder

Recuerdo de viaje: ¡Buenos días, aventureros virtuales! Hoy es viernes, 8 de mayo de 2026, y tengo muchas ganas de llevaros a un viaje espectacular al corazón de la historia portuguesa. Nuestra aventura virtual nos lleva a uno de los monumentos más famosos de Lisboa: la Torre de Belém, declarada Patrimonio de la Humanidad por la UNESCO y conocida por su majestuosa belleza, sus fascinantes leyendas y su importancia histórica. Prepárense para una exploración inmersiva de esta obra maestra arquitectónica, que en su día sirvió como puerta de entrada de Portugal al mundo. ¡Sumérjanse y descubran los secretos que se esconden tras esta mítica torre, que se ha mantenido firme a orillas del Tajo durante siglos!

Un símbolo de poder y del espíritu de descubrimiento - Construida entre 1514 y 1519 bajo el reinado del rey Manuel I, la Torre de Belém se concibió originalmente como una fortificación costera para proteger Lisboa de los ataques navales. Sin embargo, se convirtió en mucho más que una simple estructura militar. Ricamente decorada con motivos de estilo manuelino —como cuerdas retorcidas, cruces de la Orden de Cristo y esferas armilares—, la torre encarnaba la supremacía marítima de Portugal durante la Era de los Descubrimientos. Estratégicamente situada en la desembocadura del río, la Torre de Belém fue testigo de cómo flotas repletas de exploradores, especias y tesoros zarpaban hacia tierras lejanas, y les daba la bienvenida a su regreso como símbolo del alcance global de Portugal. Cuando uno imagina sus miradores, que recuerdan a las cubiertas de los barcos, y las ornamentadas decoraciones inspiradas en culturas exóticas, rápidamente queda claro cómo la torre refleja visualmente el espíritu de aventura que definió esta época.

La escultura del rinoceronte: una historia de fusión cultural - Entre las muchas historias grabadas en la piedra de este monumento, hay un detalle particularmente fascinante por descubrir: un rinoceronte tallado en la fachada norte. Esta escultura representa un rinoceronte real que fue regalado al rey Manuel I por un gobernante indio en 1515. Aunque el rinoceronte se perdió trágicamente en el mar de camino a Roma, dejó un legado indeleble. Inspiró los famosos dibujos de Alberto Durero y encontró la vida eterna en las tallas de la Torre de Belém. Este detalle aparentemente insignificante revela una verdad más amplia sobre las aventuras marítimas de Portugal: estos viajes no se limitaban a la conquista de territorios, sino que también trajeron consigo animales, ideas e intercambios culturales que alteraron para siempre el tejido de Europa.

Mitos en torno al Tajo y la Torre - Una cautivadora leyenda sobre la Torre de Belém afirma que fue construida originalmente en medio del Tajo, pero que se trasladó más cerca de la orilla tras el devastador terremoto de 1755. En realidad, la verdad reside en los sutiles cambios de la línea costera a lo largo de los siglos. La torre se construyó en una pequeña isla cerca de la costa, que se fue ampliando gradualmente y conectó la estructura con el continente. Aunque desmontar este mito no le resta encanto, la imagen de una torre que se eleva sobre el agua contribuye a su atractivo místico: un símbolo perdurable de cómo Portugal gobernó en su día los vastos océanos.

Los capítulos oscuros de la torre - Aparte de su pasado romántico y aventurero, la torre también alberga historias más sombrías. En sus últimos años, la Torre de Belém sirvió como prisión, especialmente bajo el reinado del rey Miguel I en el siglo XIX. Sus frías cámaras —destinadas originalmente al almacenamiento de armas— se reconvirtieron para encarcelar a opositores políticos y disidentes. Estos episodios inquietantes nos recuerdan que incluso los lugares grandiosos tienen su lado oscuro. Las capas contrastantes de luz y oscuridad en la historia de la torre la hacen aún más fascinante: un reflejo de las luchas y los triunfos de Portugal a lo largo del tiempo.

Un viaje arquitectónico a través del tiempo - La Torre de Belém encarna siglos de evolución arquitectónica. Bajo la dirección del arquitecto Francisco de Arruda, se integraron influencias del arte morisco, evidentes en los patrones geométricos, las cúpulas acanaladas y las elegantes arcadas que adornan su estructura. Más tarde, en el siglo XIX, los adornos románticos acentuaron su estilo manuelino, transformando la fortaleza en un festín para la vista. Al admirar los intrincados detalles, se dará cuenta de cómo la torre sirve de puente entre épocas, combinando su función defensiva con una artesanía impresionante: una auténtica cápsula del tiempo arquitectónica.

Una de las Siete Maravillas de Portugal - No es de extrañar que la Torre de Belém fuera nombrada «Una de las Siete Maravillas de Portugal» en 2007. Los turistas acuden en masa no solo por su importancia histórica, sino también por la impresionante vista panorámica que ofrece sobre el río Tajo. Miles de personas suben a su cima cada año para maravillarse ante un hito que se erige como puerta de entrada, tanto física como simbólica, al glorioso pasado de Portugal.

Una cápsula del tiempo viviente: la Torre de Belém desafía el paso del tiempo; sus muros conservan la esencia de la identidad portuguesa. Desde su papel en la Era de los Descubrimientos, pasando por su etapa como prisión, hasta su designación como Patrimonio de la Humanidad por la UNESCO, la torre encarna el coraje, la innovación y el espíritu de descubrimiento. Al entrar, se tiene la sensación de estar entrando en otro mundo, un mundo donde los ecos de viajes lejanos se mezclan con los susurros de quienes una vez recorrieron sus pasillos.

Tu puerta de entrada a la historia: la Torre de Belém no es solo un edificio, es un testimonio de la audacia, la creatividad y la resiliencia de Portugal. Tanto si te atrae su importancia histórica, su belleza arquitectónica o las leyendas que la rodean, te garantizo que saldrás de allí sintiéndote inspirado.

¡Muchas gracias por acompañarme en la aventura virtual de hoy! Mañana nos embarcaremos en un nuevo viaje para descubrir otro tesoro de nuestra historia humana compartida. Hasta entonces, te deseo un día maravilloso. Un saludo, Freddy Kalder

Je suis secrétaire chez un pédiatre. Ce soir, à 18h45, une jeune maman arrive en courant, trempée par la pluie, avec son bébé qui tousse énormément. Elle a l'air épuisée, c'est clairement une maman solo qui sort de sa journée de travail.
À la fin de la consultation, au moment de payer les 35 euros, elle se rend compte qu'elle a oublié son portefeuille dans la précipitation. Elle devient rouge de honte, les larmes montent : "Je vous laisse ma carte d'identité, je reviens demain matin à la première heure, je vous le jure."
Un monsieur en salle d'attente, en costume, lève les yeux au ciel en soupirant : "C'est toujours pareil, les gens font des enfants sans savoir s'organiser..."
Le pédiatre, qui a tout entendu, sort de son bureau. Il regarde le monsieur et dit froidement : "Ici on soigne, on ne juge pas."
Puis il se tourne vers la maman, lui fait un clin d'œil et dit : "Votre bébé a été très courageux. C'est la consultation 'premier rhume de l'année', elle est 100% offerte par le cabinet. Rentrez vite le mettre au chaud."
Je n'ai jamais vu un tel soulagement dans les yeux d'une mère.

Habib Ahmad Tulungagung Sudah Mengetahui Jam Wafatnya

Wali memang tidak takut mati. Bahkan ketika umurnya akan penuh (wafat), mereka sudah menyiapkan diri. Termasuk Habib Ahmad Salim Al-Muhdlor, Desa Domasan, Kaligawen, Tulungagung, Jawa Timur.

Kepada Kiai Khoirul (seorang ulama), Habib Ahmad pernah menyatakan bahwa ia, pada jam 12 siang saat bertemu Kiai Khoirul, akan meninggal. Terang saja Kiai Khoirul tidak percaya begitu saja.

"Mau meninggal kok tidak pakai pendahuluan Bib, sakit atau apa begitu," kata Kiai Khoirul.

Mereka berdua masih ngobrol, dan tanpa ada tanda wafat sama sakali, Habib Ahmad tetap saja asyik ngobrol bersama Kiai Koirul sampai 11.30, hanya kurang 30an menit seperti dikatakan.

"Ini kurang lima menit loh, Bib," tanya Kiai Khoirul.

"Iya, ini Izra'il sudah datang," jawab Habib Ahmad, "tapi sebelum meninggal, aku ingin buat perjanjian sama kamu," lanjut Habib Ahmad.

"Perjanjian apa Bib?" Kiai Khoirul makin dibuat heran, karena hanya kurang 5 menitan beliau akan meninggal.

Habib Ahmad membuat perjanjian ke Kiai Khoirul. Ini perjanjiannnya:

Bila kamu di akhirat besok lebih nikmat dari aku, maka aku ikut kamu, tapi bila aku lebih nikmat, kamu harus ikut aku. 

Sebelum seminggu kamu meninggal, aku akan akan datang memberitahumu.

Benar saja, setelah kesepakatan itu diucapakan, Habib Ahmad langsung meninggal. Tiba-tiba saja beliau terlihat seperti lemas, bersandar ke ke tembok dan wafat seketika. Innalillah wa inna ilahi raji'un.

Habib Ahmad Salim Al-Muhdlor Tulungagung wafat pas seperti dikatakan, jam 12 persis. Dan, sebelum Kiai Khoirul wafat pun, beliau memang ditemui Habib Ahmad (dalam kondisi setengah sadar dan tidak) kalau sepekan lagi ia harus siap dijemput Izra'il dengan jalan kepleset di rumah.

***

Cerita lain juga datang dari Mbah Dimyathi Comal, guru Habib Luthfi bin Yahya, yang pernah memberitahukan waktu wafatnya dengan bahasa pengantin.

"Bib, seminggu lagi akan jadi pengantin. Itu tempatnya," kata Mbah Dimyathi ke Habib Luthfi sambil menunjuk calon lokasi pemakaman.

Beliau berpesan ke Habib Luthfi agar orang-orang yang mengiringi jenazah membaca shalawat Burdah.
